## Natural history notes

A small freshwater ramshorn snail characterized by a flattened, coiled shell with rounded whorls that spiral in a single plane, giving it a disk-like appearance. In Florida, the Mesa Ramshorn is found in ponds, marshes, ditches, canals, slow streams, wetland pools, and vegetated freshwater edges where algae, biofilm, and decaying plant material are available. It grazes on algae, detritus, and microbial films on submerged surfaces, helping recycle nutrients while serving as prey for fishes, turtles, aquatic insects, crayfish, and wading birds.
